CLAIM | "Both spellings name the same file, so accepting both is not a guess and costs no precision. So ``fan_in`` — accumulated over ``dep_edges`` keys — still counts each file exactly once, and the top fan-in table cannot shift for a bookkeeping reason." | _PyNaming._build | KEPT | The _build method registers aliases and the docstring describes the intention.

CLAIM | "The alias lives ONLY in its own center's view, and it is that center's own path prefix, so it cannot widen what a shell file is eligible to bind. An alias also never displaces a real module: if some file genuinely owns that spelling in this view, the alias is dropped." | _PyNaming._build | BROKEN | Line: `if spelling not in by_name:` — the condition checks if the alias spelling is not already a module name in the view, but the docstring says "if some file genuinely owns that spelling in this view, the alias is dropped." The code does drop the alias if the spelling is already in `by_name`, which is consistent. However, the docstring says "if some file genuinely owns that spelling in this view" — but the alias spelling is the repo-root form (e.g., `TCT_app.controller.danger_gate`), which would never be a module name in the view because the view uses package-relative names. So the condition `spelling not in by_name` will always be true for aliases, and the alias is always added. This contradicts "if some file genuinely owns that spelling in this view, the alias is dropped" because such a file cannot exist in this view. The promise is vacuously true but misleading.

CLAIM | "Any None here means a worker silently dropped a file — recompute inline rather than shipping a short/misaligned list to the clone passes." | _per_file_pass | KEPT | The fallback loop handles None entries.
CLAIM | "No usable pool (sandbox, spawn failure, unpicklable payload): the serial path is always correct, just slower." | _compute | KEPT | The except block falls back to serial.

CLAIM | "wiki_on = wiki_enabled(wiki) and docs_on   # wiki edges need documents indexed" | build_index | BROKEN | Line: `wiki_on = wiki_enabled(wiki) and docs_on`. The docstring for wiki_enabled says it defaults to False, but the comment says wiki edges need documents indexed. However, the code forces wiki_on to be False if docs_on is False, even if wiki is True. This contradicts the docstring of wiki_enabled which says the explicit argument wins. The docstring says "Explicit argument wins; else ``DAEDALUS_INDEX_WIKI``; else False." But here, if docs_on is False, wiki_on is forced False regardless of the explicit wiki argument. So the claim that explicit argument wins is not fully honored when documents are off.

CLAIM | "SCOPE: the declared center (what this project IS) plus .daedalusignore (exceptions carved within it). Everything else in the repo is SHELL — real source, but not this project's code: vendored trees, spec copies, generated skeletons." | build_index | KEPT | The function uses scope which handles center and ignore.
CLAIM | "Shell files are deliberately still collected and still parsed: they stay" | build_index | KEPT | The function continues to collect all files.
